newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly higher, July down on spreads.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly higher, July down on spreads.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended a quiet session mostly higher, led by soybeans, amid forecasts for more rain in the eastern Corn Belt, traders said.
Meteorologists predicted weekend rains in the eastern Corn Belt but long-range forecasts suggested a drier week ahead.
Soils in parts of the eastern Corn Belt are already saturated, so more rain was viewed as a hindrance to the developing corn crop, traders said.
World supply situations were also drawing attention. Floor sources noted the U.S. agricultural attache in South Africa said heavy rainfall would likely damage the corn crop there.

Slow farmer selling in the country and talk of supply tightness in the western Corn Belt also boosted futures. Cash grain dealers said farmer selling interest was at a virtual standstill on Friday amid signs that prices are beginning to recover after recent weakness.

Bear spreading late weighed on the July contract which ended a shade lower. Trade sources said the market was beginning to put in a weather premium in the December and was growing less concerned about old crop supplies.
Corn ended 2-1/4 cents higher to down 1/4 cent, with July off 1/4 at $2.74 a bushel.
Commercials supported the market much of the session. Cargill Inc bought four million bushels July and 3.5 million December, pit sources said.
Smith Barney bought three million December while LIT sold three million December.
In options trade, Continental Grain bought 400 December $2.60 calls at 14-3/4 cents and sold 400 December $3.00 calls at six cents. CIS bought 300 September $2.70 calls at 9-1/2 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 35,000 contracts, below Thursday's actual volume of 39,238.
